display_name: Deliver a background job completion to its role inbox
description: Push a finished background job's outcome into the durable role-addressed inbox of the session that started it. This is the wake half of the background-job completion contract, whose durable/retrievable half is job_service::get_job and job_service::list_unreached_job_completions. Submitted automatically by AsyncJobManager when the originating flow carries a completion_route_role stamp; it is not a verb callers normally invoke by hand. Only a FLEET caller is addressable: a solet call bridge mints a fresh session per open, so durable delivery keys on the DURABLE ROLE that PlatformSurface resolved from the launcher-exported AGENT_SESSION_ID at dispatch time. A bare-shell CLI caller resolves to no role, is never stamped, and keeps the pull path — coverage is partial by construction. Delivery reuses the persist-first role dispatch (dispatch_role_send), so the envelope is written durably BEFORE delivery and an offline holder yields delivery='queued_for_replay' rather than a hard failure. On a measured hand-off the job's completion_reach is upgraded to role_inbox_delivered, which removes it from the unreached drain; a delivery or stamp that fails leaves the earlier bridge_dispatch_no_return_path marker standing so the drain still lists the job. The delivered message embeds job_id, the originating plugin.verb, the terminal status and the payload itself (truncated with an explicit notice and a get_job pointer when oversized) so the recipient can act without a second lookup. The sender is a fixed system sentinel, never the caller: a completion has no human author, and resolving one from the flow would name the recipient as its own sender.
embedding_description: Deliver the result of a finished asynchronous background job into the durable inbox of the durable role that started it, waking that session instead of leaving the outcome to be polled. Covers fleet callers whose dispatch carried a role; unaddressable callers keep the pull path. Errors are delivered the same way successes are.

result_processor_customizations.action_label: Job completion delivered to role inbox
result_processor_customizations.result_description: thread_id, message_id, the delivery channel (queued_notification / queued_wake / queued_watcher / queued_for_replay), the resolved (resolved_agent_id, resolved_agent_instance_id, resolved_session_label) the role pointed at, plus reach_stamped: whether the job's completion_reach was upgraded to role_inbox_delivered. reach_stamped=false alongside a successful delivery means the push landed but the marker write did not, so the job stays listed by list_unreached_job_completions and may be reported a second time — over-reporting is deliberate, because losing a completion is not recoverable and repeating one is.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Confirm which role received the completion and over which delivery channel. queued_for_replay is a SUCCESS (the envelope is durable and the repair drain re-delivers), not a failure. If reach_stamped is false, say plainly that the job will still appear in the unreached drain despite having been delivered.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Resolves the routed role via the agent_role_binding state table and dispatches a persist-first role send carrying the finished job's status and payload, then stamps the job's completion_reach.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: missing_arguments: name or job_id was empty — the routing stamp or the job id did not reach the verb, and no delivery was attempted. peer_role_vacant: no agent_role_binding row exists for the routed role; the holder released it or never claimed it, so the completion stays retrievable via job_service instead. peer_role_malformed: the binding exists but has no agent_instance_id (re-claim via peer_claim_role). bridge.not_running: start_interface has not completed. state_service_unavailable: the state_service is not bound on this solet. In every one of these the job's own row and payloads are already persisted and the completion remains retrievable with job_service::get_job.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: Retrieve the outcome directly with service_interface::job_service::get_job using the job_id the dispatch returned, or drain everything undelivered with service_interface::job_service::list_unreached_job_completions. peer_role_vacant / peer_role_malformed: have the intended holder re-claim the role with peer_claim_role, which restores delivery for subsequent completions. Do not re-run the original job to recover a result that is already stored.
